hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 3]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $94^\circ$ and $37^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 94^\circ - 37^\circ = 49^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is thirty-seven degrees. Angle B is ninety-four degrees. Angle C is forty-nine degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $DEF$ has angle measures of $37^\circ$ and $94^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 37^\circ - 94^\circ = 49^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle DEF$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle D E F. Angle D is thirty-seven degrees. Angle E is ninety-four degrees. Angle F is forty-nine degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $IHG$ has angle measures of $49^\circ$ and $94^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 49^\circ - 94^\circ = 37^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle IHG$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle G H I. Angle I is thirty-seven degrees. Angle H is ninety-four degrees. Angle G is forty-nine degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, *both* triangles are similar to $\triangle ABC$.
